path.title: TESTED_ON [paper-A p-0010] All adsorption experiments for lactic, succinic, and citric acids were conducted using a standardized protocol
TESTED_ON [paper-A p-0010] All adsorption experiments for lactic, succinic, and citric acids were conducted using a standardized protocol
TESTED_ON [paper-A p-0010] All adsorption experiments for lactic, succinic, and citric acids were conducted using a standardized protocol
HAS_RESULT [paper-A p-0039] the specific surface area of the MGO was determined to be 37.94 m2/g
HAS_RESULT [paper-A p-0040] parallel textural characterization was conducted on a magnetic activated carbon (AC) reference, which exhibited a slightly higher surface area (40.38 m2/g)
HAS_RESULT [paper-A p-0039] the average pore radius was found to be 4.12 nm
HAS_RESULT [paper-A p-0055] The maximum adsorption capacity of MGO for lactic acid (334.45 mg/g) is highly competitive
HAS_RESULT [paper-A p-0040] its maximum adsorption capacity for lactic acid was substantially lower (q max = 74.6 mg/g)
HAS_RESULT [paper-A p-0045] the overall mean adsorption capacity (Q e) was determined as 188.6 mg/g for MGO-based and 67.8 mg/g for AC-based adsorbents
HAS_RESULT [paper-A p-0048] the overall mean adsorption capacity was determined to be 213 mg/g for MGO-based and 73.7 mg/g for AC-based adsorbents
HAS_RESULT [paper-A p-0051] the activated carbon-based adsorbent exhibits a slightly higher adsorption capacity than the MGO composite
HAS_RESULT [paper-A p-0059] The experimental data for all acids exhibited an excellent fit with the PSO model (R 2 > 0.99)
HAS_RESULT [paper-A p-0059] The rate constants (k 2) were determined as 0.007, 0.0023, and 0.0019 g/mg·min
HAS_RESULT [paper-A p-0063] R L values for all investigated acids on both adsorbents across the studied concentration range (10–100 g/L) were between 2.3 × 10–6 and 2.8 × 10–3
HAS_RESULT [paper-A p-0067] The capacity retention rates after the fifth cycle were found to be 87.8% for succinic acid and 84.2% for citric acid.
HAS_RESULT [paper-B p-0035] The carbon content increases to 55.61 wt.%, whereas the oxygen content decreases to 40.79 wt.%.
HAS_RESULT [paper-B p-0035] The carbon content increases to 55.61 wt.%, whereas the oxygen content decreases to 40.79 wt.%.
HAS_RESULT [paper-B p-0038] the HA-rGO composite shows an increase in Σ(COOH + OH) to 5.47 mmol/g compared with the initial humic acid (5.00 mmol/g)
HAS_RESULT [paper-B p-0037] For the HA-rGO composite, the O/C ratio decreases to 0.73.
HAS_RESULT [paper-B p-0058] The residual mass of the initial humic acid is 59.21%, whereas that of the HA-rGO composite increases to 70.03%.
TESTED_ON [paper-B p-0028] Phenol adsorption was evaluated as a preliminary functional test of the synthesized HA-rGO composite.
HAS_RESULT [paper-B p-0094] The maximum adsorption capacity calculated according to the Langmuir model was 7.10 mg/g for HA–rGO
HAS_RESULT [paper-B p-0093] For rGO, the Langmuir and Freundlich models showed comparable agreement with the experimental data
HAS_RESULT [paper-B p-0099] The pseudo-first-order model exhibited a marginally higher R2 value of 0.9973 compared with 0.9968 for the pseudo-second-order model.
